primitives.name: MoME Transformer Block
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - MoME block: H'_l = MSA(LN(H_{l-1})) + H_{l-1}; H_l = MoME-FFN(LN(H'_l)) + H'_l.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H_l': 'hidden representation at layer l, dimensionless', "H'_l": 'intermediate representation after MSA, dimensionless', 'MSA': 'multi-head self-attention across modalities, dimensionless', 'LN': 'layer normalization, dimensionless', 'MoME-FFN': 'modality-specific feedforward network, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Shared attention aligns modalities; experts preserve modality-specific features; fusion occurs only in top layers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When modality-specific experts fail to capture cross-modal dependencies in early layers.

layer2.mapping: The MoME block mirrors GSE's dual/fusion encoder logic where early layers process modality-specific signals and later layers integrate them for reasoning.

primitives.name: Stagewise Pretraining Recipe
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Stagewise pre-training**: (1) train V-FFN + shared self-attention on image-only data via BEiT masked image modeling; (2) freeze those, train L-FFN on text-only data via MLM; (3) initialize full model and run vision-language pre-training with three losses: image-text contrastive (ITC), image-text matching (ITM), masked language modeling (MLM).
primitives.assumptions: Sequential training improves generalization by transferring modality-specific knowledge before joint learning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If joint pretraining starts without prior modality-specific learning, performance degrades due to lack of modality alignment.

layer2.mapping: Enables GSI to build robust priors from sparse tracking data by first learning visual patterns, then textual semantics, finally combining both.
layer2.telemetry: Per-layer loss curves show convergence order of V→L→VL stages.

primitives.name: Deterministic Expert Routing
primitives.verbatim_quote: Routing is deterministic by input modality and layer index: image/text-only inputs use V/L experts throughout; image-text pairs use V+L experts in bottom layers and the VL expert in the top layers (top-2 layers base, top-3 large).
primitives.assumptions: Fixed routing suffices for modality interaction; no need for learned gating mechanisms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In scenarios involving more than two modalities (e.g., tracking), fixed routing may underperform compared to adaptive routing.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE’s dynamic mode switching—wherein simple queries trigger dual-encoder paths, while complex matchups invoke fusion encoders.
layer2.telemetry: Layer-wise expert usage frequency reflects query complexity and modality dominance.

reasoning_traces.think:
The MoME architecture integrates vision-language processing through a hybrid of shared attention and modality-specific experts. In early layers, image-only or text-only inputs activate respective experts, preserving modality-specific representations. As layers deepen, image-text pairs engage both V+L and VL experts, enabling contextual fusion. This structure supports dual-encoder retrieval (linear-time) and fusion-encoder reasoning (non-linear). The stagewise pretraining ensures that each modality learns independently before joint training, improving robustness. The deterministic routing strategy simplifies implementation but lacks adaptability to new modalities. For GSI, this translates into Bayesian updating over dual-mode encodings for historical play inference. For GSE, it enables rapid retrieval followed by deep reasoning depending on input complexity. Failure modes include misalignment in early layers or insufficient fusion depth for nuanced matchups.
